why: Winter waterfall-ice route in a South Fork drainage near Cody, no glacier involved, climbed in the cold season.
Remote Wind River basin route; only a hint that crampons helped on the approach, nothing says what the approach crosses.
Winter ice-and-mixed route on a Jackson Hole buttress, not a glacier line.
Same Jackson Hole buttress sector, a winter mixed climb with ice, no glacier.
The one-day approach is described via the Teepe Glacier while the usual alternative is from the Lower Saddle, and snow lingers on the approach.
Rock ridge beside the Ellingwood Couloir reached up Garnet Canyon's south fork, where snow and crampons are advised.
Frozen waterfall pillar climbed in winter in Teton Canyon, no glacier.
The start is reached by snow to the Buck-Static notch and the east-face descent is snow, with no glacier described.
Buck Mountain's rock lines carry no glacier, but sources only mention early-season snow and I found nothing on this line.
Rock arete approached from Garnet Canyon and the Lower Saddle, no glacier on that approach, but I found no snow detail.
Traverse over Teewinot, Owen and the Grand crosses snowfields and the Koven snow descent, and may touch the Teton Glacier area.
Modern line starts from the midway ledge reached from Amphitheater Lake, and Glacier Gulch is only a name; snow need not be crossed but unconfirmed.
Rock ridge between snow couloirs on Middle Teton, which holds snow much of the season.
North approach couloir is snow or talus depending on season and there is no glacier on Cody Peak.
Camp access crosses snow on the Teepe Glacier, which is a real glacier, though its crevasse hazard on this walk is unclear.
Reached from the Lower Saddle or the Teepe Glacier side near Glencoe Col, and snow near the base is only described as early-season.
The col crossing is steep snow all year, and parties may drop onto the Middle Teton Glacier, though the main line is the dike.
Reached from the Lower Saddle with no glacier, but snow on the ridge is described only as early-to-mid season.
Peak is beside the Falling Ice Glacier on Moran, and I could not confirm what this line actually crosses.
Cirque of the Towers rock route reached on trail, with a snow patch mentioned only as a landmark at the base.
Ridge begins at the Teton Glacier moraine rather than on the ice, with ice axe and crampons for upper snowfields.
Garnet south fork rock ridge, where the route text calls for crampons and axe for the moderate snow.
Snow couloir up to about 45 degrees on the south side of Middle Teton, separate from its glacier route.
Approach goes up the Enclosure's snow and ice couloir off the Valhalla Traverse, no glacier.
Mixed variation on the Enclosure's ice couloir, no glacier involved.
Snow and ice couloir on the Enclosure, no glacier involved.
Southeast snow couloir on Fremont Peak described as a snow climb up to about 45 degrees, not on the Upper Fremont Glacier.
Dry-tooling crag with no glacier, but I found no detail about snow on the approach.
Wall sits about 500 yards beside the Grasshopper Glacier's toe and the approach is not described as crossing it.
Absaroka peak with no glacier on its west face, snow described only as early season and in a descent gully.
Route passes the end of the Teton Glacier and climbs an upper snowfield needing axe and crampons.
Enclosure rock route off the Valhalla Traverse, no glacier, snow gear only conditional.
